## [Project 8 : Pima Diabetes Prediction]{.underline} {style="color:steelblue;"}

Project description:

### Loading relevant libraries

```{r}
# loading libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
```

### Loading Pima dataset

```{r}
pima <- read_csv("D:/R ANALYTICS/Practice Datasets/diabetes.csv",
                 show_col_types = FALSE)
cat('Data loaded successfully')
```

**Inspecting data structure and variable data types:**

```{r}
pima |> head()
```

```{r}
# Checking dataset dimension and missing values: 768 rows and 9 columns
dim(pima)
```

```{r}
# checking the data types of the columns in the pima dataset
pima |> map_chr(typeof)
```

### **Quantifying missing data to inform preprocessing decisions:**

```{r}
# checking missing data :  
mis_count <- colSums(is.na(pima))
# let's convert it to a nice table
mis_count |>  enframe(
  name = "variable",
  value = "count"
)
```

**Checking for biologically impossible values and handling them:**

```{r}
# using the map function to check for minimum values in columns
pima |> 
  map_dbl(min)
```

**You could see there are zero glucose values,blood pressure, insulin and bmi: these are biologically impossible and must be treated as missing data.**

```{r}
# replaces NA where biological impossible values exist:
impo_bio_cols <- c('SkinThickness','Glucose','Insulin','BMI','BloodPressure')
pima[impo_bio_cols] <- map(pima[impo_bio_cols],\(x) ifelse(x==0,NA,x))
```

```{r}
# let's check if the minimimum values ares till zero
pima |> 
  map_dbl(\(x) min(x,na.rm = TRUE))
```

**Now that we have no zeros, let's check for missing values:**

```{r}
colSums(is.na(pima))
```

```{r}
# visualizing missingness
library(naniar)
```

```{r fig.dpi=300, fig.height=7, fig.width=14}

pima |>
  rename(
    "Pregnancies"        = Pregnancies,
    "Glucose (mg/dL)"    = Glucose,
    "Blood Pressure"     = BloodPressure,
    "Skin Thickness"     = SkinThickness,
    "Insulin (μU/mL)"    = Insulin,
    "BMI (kg/m²)"        = BMI,
    "Pedigree Function"  = DiabetesPedigreeFunction,
    "Age (years)"        = Age,
    "Outcome"            = Outcome
  ) |>
  vis_miss() +
  labs(
    title   = "Missingness Pattern — Pima Diabetes Dataset",
    caption = "Source: @SambugAnalytics"
  ) +
  theme(
    text = element_text(family = "serif", size = 13),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11),
    plot.caption  = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

```{r}
# Missingness by diabetic status
pima |>
  group_by(Outcome) |>
  summarise(across(impo_bio_cols, ~ sum(is.na(.x))))
```

```{r}
# checking if pattern exist in missing data :
mcar_test(pima)
```

**Median imputation stratified by outcome**

Little's MCAR test was statistically significant (χ² = 166.97, df = 69, p \< 0.001), indicating that missingness is not completely at random. Stratified median imputation by outcome group was applied as a clinically defensible approach, preserving biological differences between diabetic and non-diabetic patients.

```{r}
pima <- pima |>
  group_by(Outcome) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(impo_bio_cols), ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), .x))) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
# checking if there is any NAs 
colSums(is.na(pima))
```

### Let's do some correlations:

```{r}
# library for correlation analysis
library(correlation)
library(corrplot)
```

```{r fig.dpi=300, fig.height=7, fig.width=10}

library(reshape2)

# compute correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- pima |>
  cor(method = "spearman") |>
  round(2)

# convert to long format for ggplot
cor_long <- cor_matrix |>
  melt()

ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = value)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = value), size = 3.5, family = "serif") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low      = "#2471a3",
    mid      = "white",
    high     = "#c0392b",
    midpoint = 0,
    limits   = c(-1, 1),
    name     = "Spearman\nCorrelation"
  ) +
  labs(
    title    = "Spearman Correlation Heatmap — Pima Diabetes Dataset",
    subtitle = "Red = positive correlation | Blue = negative correlation",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = NULL,
    caption  = "Source: @SambugAnalytics"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    text           = element_text(family = "serif", size = 13),
    plot.title     = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle  = element_text(colour = "#555555", size = 11),
    axis.text.x    = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 11),
    axis.text.y    = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.position = "right",
    panel.grid     = element_blank(),
    plot.caption   = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

Glucose and Insulin showed the strongest correlations with diabetic outcome (ρ = 0.49 and 0.56 respectively), consistent with their central role in T2DM pathophysiology. BMI and SkinThickness were highly inter-correlated (ρ = 0.59), suggesting multicollinearity that may affect coefficient interpretation in regression models. The strong Age-Pregnancies correlation (ρ = 0.61) reflects demographic patterning rather than biological causation.

**Clinical Threshold Flagging** : **code for flagging data**

```{r}
pima_flagged <- pima |>
  mutate(
    # Glucose risk tier (WHO OGTT criteria)
    glucose_category = case_when(
      Glucose < 140 ~ "Normal",
      Glucose >= 140 & Glucose < 200 ~ "Prediabetic",
      Glucose >= 200 ~ "Diabetic"
    ),
    
    # BMI classification (WHO)
    bmi_category = case_when(
      BMI < 18.5 ~ "Underweight",
      BMI >= 18.5 & BMI < 25 ~ "Normal",
      BMI >= 25 & BMI < 30 ~ "Overweight",
      BMI >= 30 ~ "Obese"
    ),
    
    # Blood pressure (JNC guidelines)
    bp_category = case_when(
      BloodPressure < 80 ~ "Normal",
      BloodPressure >= 80 & BloodPressure < 90 ~ "Elevated",
      BloodPressure >= 90 ~ "Hypertensive"
    ),
    
    # Age risk group
    age_group = case_when(
      Age < 30 ~ "Young adult (< 30)",
      Age >= 30 & Age < 45 ~ "Middle age (30–44)",
      Age >= 45  ~ "High risk (≥ 45)"
    ),
    
    # Insulin status
    insulin_status = case_when(
      Insulin <= 166 ~ "Normal",
      Insulin > 166  ~ "Hyperinsulinaemia"
    ),
    
    # Pregnancy risk
    pregnancy_risk = case_when(
      Pregnancies == 0  ~ "Never pregnant",
      Pregnancies >= 1 & Pregnancies < 3 ~ "Low (1–2)",
      Pregnancies >= 3  ~ "Elevated (≥ 3)"
    )
  ) |>
  # convert all new variables to ordered factors
  mutate(
    glucose_category = factor(glucose_category,
                              levels = c("Normal", "Prediabetic", "Diabetic")),
    bmi_category     = factor(bmi_category,
                              levels = c("Underweight", "Normal",
                                         "Overweight", "Obese")),
    bp_category      = factor(bp_category,
                              levels = c("Normal", "Elevated", "Hypertensive")),
    age_group        = factor(age_group,
                              levels = c("Young adult (< 30)",
                                         "Middle age (30–44)",
                                         "High risk (≥ 45)")),
    insulin_status   = factor(insulin_status,
                              levels = c("Normal", "Hyperinsulinaemia")),
    pregnancy_risk   = factor(pregnancy_risk,
                              levels = c("Never pregnant", "Low (1–2)",
                                         "Elevated (≥ 3)"))
  )
```

```{r}
# filtering our summary columns 
flagged_data <- pima_flagged |> 
  select(c(Outcome,glucose_category:pregnancy_risk)) |> 
  mutate(
    Outcome = factor(Outcome,labels = c("Non-diabetic","Diabetic"))
  )
```

**Comparison of Clinical Thresholds by Outcome**

```{r}
# let's load the gtsummary package for the graceful handling of this task
library(gtsummary)
# creating the table
flagged_data |> 
  tbl_summary(
    by = Outcome,
    statistic  = all_categorical() ~ "{n} ({p}%)",
    missing  = "no" ,
    label = list(
      glucose_category~ "Glucose Category",
      bmi_category~ "BMI Category",
      bp_category ~ "bp Category"
    )) |> 
  add_p() |>
  add_overall() |>
  bold_labels() |>
  modify_header(label ~ "**Clinical Variable**") |>
  modify_caption("**Clinical Threshold Distribution by Diabetes Status**") |> 
  as_gt() |> #creates a gt object to allow the table.width fun to work: optional
  gt::tab_options(table.width = "100%")

```

**Comparison of variables stratified by Outcome**

```{r}
pima |> 
  mutate(Outcome = factor(Outcome, levels=c(1,0), labels = c("Diabetic","Non-diabetic"))) |> 
  tbl_summary(
    by = Outcome,
    statistic = list(
      all_categorical()~"{n} ({p}%)",
      all_continuous()~"{median}({IQR})"
    ),
    missing = 'no',
    
  ) |> 
  add_p() |> 
  modify_header(label~"**Variables**") |> 
  modify_caption("**Comparison of continous variable stratified by Outcome**") |> 
  as_gt() |> 
  gt::tab_options(table.width = "100%")
```

```{r}
model1 <- glm(
  formula = Outcome~Glucose+BMI+DiabetesPedigreeFunction+Insulin+Age+Pregnancies,
              family = "binomial",
              data = pima)
tbl_regression(model1, exponentiate = TRUE) |> 
  as_gt() |> 
  gt::tab_options(table.width = "100%")
```
